case_name: Dantuluri Ram Raju and Others v State of Andhra Pradesh and Another
respondent:
State of Andhra Pradesh and Another
Supreme Court of India

16 December 1971
C.A. No. 223 of 1970. Appeal from the judgment and order dated March 27, 1969 of the Andhra Pradesh High Court in Writ Petition No. 998 of 1969. AND ORIGINAL JURISDICTION : Writ Petition No. 251 of 197 1.
The Judgment was delivered by : Hans Raj Khanna, J.
1.  Appeal from the judgment and order dated March 27, 1969 of the Andhra Pradesh High Court in Writ Petition No. 998 of 1969.
2.  The vires of the Andhra Pradesh (Krishna and Godavari Delta Area) Drainage Cess Act, 1968 (Act No. 11 of 1968), hereinafter referred to as the Act, has been challenged in Civil Appeal No. 223 of 1970 as well as in Writ Petition No. 25 1 of 1971. Civil Appeal No. 223 has been filed on a certificate granted by the Andhra Pradesh High Court against the judgment of that Court whereby petition u/art. 226 of the Constitution of India presented on behalf of the eight appellants to assail the vires of the
facts: The vires of the Andhra Pradesh (Krishna and Godavari Delta Area) Drainage Cess Act, 1968 has been challenged in Civil Appeal No. 223 of 1970 as well as in Writ Petition No. 251 of 1971.
The appellants in the civil appeal belong to different Taluks of the West Godavari District and own extensive areas of land in that district.
Petitioners Nos. 1 to 38 in the writ petition are residents of Tenneru within the area of Vijayawada Taluk.
The respondents were consequently permitted to file an affidavit in this Court.
issues: Vires of the Andhra Pradesh (Krishna and Godavari Delta Area) Drainage Cess Act, 1968
Levy and collection of drainage cess
respondent_arguments: The respondents were consequently permitted to file an affidavit in this Court.
holding: The provisions of the impugned Act are not violative of art. 14 of the Constitution.
There is no substance in the contention advanced on behalf of the appellants that the right of appeal provided by s. 5 of the Act is illusory.
The argument that there has been excessive delegation of the legislative power in the matter of determining the rate of cess is equally devoid of force.
No authority has been cited before us to show that even though maximum limit of the tax has been prescribed, the absence of a minimum limit vitiates the taxing statute.
